DOMAIN: Account / Master Data

- Partners: partner_name, partner_type, alliance_tier. Belongs to Account.

Source: attached 'Brillio Agentic CRM · Workflow Design' HTML, ingested as prototype/design evidence. The model spans 4 business areas, 9 pursuit-to-delivery stages, 13 object lifecycles, ~230 distinct CRM objects, 20 owner roles, and a 28-agent agentic layer.

BUSINESS AREAS (4)
- Sales: Marketing, Sales, GTM, Sales Ops, Alliances — demand, deals, renewals
- Delivery: Delivery + Talent — projects, staffing, quality, time-to-value
- Operations: Finance, Legal, Data Governance — money, contracts, controls
- Leadership: Managers and executives — inspection, governance, escalations

PROCESS STAGES (9, the pursuit-to-delivery spine)
- 1. Opportunity Signal Generation (70 workflows): Surface and capture every signal that could turn into a future deal — inbound web leads, event scans, partner referrals, ABM target accounts, campaign engagement, and email/meeting signals from existing accounts. Purpose: never miss a potential opportunity and route each signal to the right Markets / Practice / Marketing owner with the right context.
- 2. Opportunity Qualification (27 workflows): Convert raw signals into qualified opportunities by validating budget, authority, need, and timing, and by tagging the motion (new business, renewal, expansion, or re-compete). Purpose: focus pursuit effort on deals that have a real chance of closing and lock in the right playbook before any solutioning starts.
- 3. Solution Strategy (13 workflows): Translate the customer need into a Brillio offering — pick the right archetype (custom build, accelerator, partnered, platform-led), choose the lead Practice, align Markets context, and decide whether partners are needed. Purpose: give the pursuit team a clear technical and commercial direction before estimating, so every downstream artifact rolls up to one story.
- 4. Deal Shaping (32 workflows): Build the proposal artifacts: estimate effort and team mix, draft the Statement of Work, structure the FRF (Field Resource Forecast) demand with location-of-work requirements, line up partner contributions, and define the win plan. Purpose: produce a defensible, deliverable offer that survives internal pricing review and earns customer sign-off.
- 5. Commercial Structuring (22 workflows): Negotiate price, terms, MSA/SOW language, payment milestones, IP ownership, and risk allocation; route through Legal, Finance, and Compliance for sign-off. Purpose: land a contract that protects margin, manages risk, and clears every required gate before signature.
- 6. Pipeline & Forecast (25 workflows): Roll qualified opportunities into a forecasted pipeline (best case / committed / closed), continuously update probability, expected close date, and bookings split (new vs. renewal vs. expansion), and govern the renewal calendar. Purpose: give leadership a credible view of revenue trajectory and focus sales hygiene on the deals that actually move the number.
- 7. Sales-to-Delivery Handoff (21 workflows): Transition signed work from sales to delivery — confirm SOW, resource the FRF, schedule kickoff, set governance cadence, open the risk register, and restate customer expectations to the delivery team. Purpose: start delivery with zero ambiguity and prevent the post-close "black hole" between contract signature and project kickoff.
- 8. Delivery Validation (39 workflows): Watch the project's first 30 / 60 / 90 days for health signals: staffing fit, scope creep, customer NPS, milestone burn-down, and margin variance against the sold model. Purpose: catch trouble early — before it shows up in financials — and confirm that the delivery team can keep the promise sales made.
- 9. Account Expansion (27 workflows): Mine the live account for renewal, cross-sell, upsell, and platform-extension moves; surface white space, map new buying centers, and trigger the right renewal workflows on the right calendar. Purpose: grow customer lifetime value by treating delivery itself as the next sales motion, not a separate disconnected phase.

OBJECT LIFECYCLES (13 — the core entity families)
- Events [sales] (9 workflows): Industry / customer event calendar, speaker & abstract management, pre / at / post-event nurture.
- Campaigns [sales] (16 workflows): Target account list governance, ABM / campaign design, execution, attribution and ROI.
- Solutions [sales] (19 workflows): Solution catalog, archetype playbooks, battle-cards, value-prop, win-rate / margin tracking.
- Leads [sales] (14 workflows): ICP, lead capture, MQL → SAL → SQL hand-off, scoring, nurture, recycling, SLA governance.
- Accounts [sales] (36 workflows): Tiering, plan, whitespace, account health, dedup, plus data governance and inbound signals on accounts.
- Contacts [sales] (8 workflows): Stakeholder & exec-sponsor maps, contact hygiene, buying-committee roles, refresh / departure tracking.
- Opportunities [sales] (36 workflows): Creation, MEDDPICC qualification, stage advancement, competitor capture, deal review, win / loss.
- Contracts [sales] (24 workflows): MSA / SOW / amendment / change order, T&C deviation, e-signature, repository, partner agreements.
- Partners [sales] (20 workflows): Partner coverage, deal registration, joint pipeline, partner-sourced revenue, MDF, alliance scorecard.
- Forecasts [sales] (19 workflows): Forecast categories, weekly snapshots, coverage ratio, accuracy, hygiene, deal inspection.
- Projects [delivery] (23 workflows): Charter, baseline, kickoff, RAG, milestones, WSR, steerco, EAC / ETC, change orders, closeout.
- Talent [delivery] (34 workflows): FRF, bench, ramp, skill-gap / certification, attrition risk, utilization, staffing.
- Revenue & Billing [delivery] (18 workflows): Revenue recognition (ASC 606), bookings vs billings, gross margin, leakage, AR aging, monthly close.

## AREA: Delivery
### Stage 1: Opportunity Signal Generation
- [Talent] Maintain resource skill profile — object: Resource Profile; trigger: New hire; certification; project completion; owners: Talent; agents: VANGUARD; kind: action
  Capture and refresh resource skills, certifications, and experience tags in Talent system
- [Talent] Capture talent location and work-mode profile — object: Resource Profile (Location); trigger: New hire; location change; annual refresh; owners: Talent; agents: VANGUARD, TIDE; kind: trigger
  Capture and refresh each resource's primary location (city, country, region, timezone), reporting / home office, and work-mode preference (remote / hybrid / on-site); used to match talent to FRF demand and to compute travel + bill-to implications
- [Talent] Capture willingness-to-relocate profile — object: Resource Profile (Relocation); trigger: Annual refresh; resource-initiated update; owners: Talent; agents: VANGUARD, TIDE; kind: trigger
  Capture each resource's willingness-to-relocate — eligible destinations (country / city list), duration tolerance (short-term, long-term, permanent), conditions (family, dependents, schooling), visa / work-authorization constraints, and earliest available date; refresh annually and on life-event triggers
- [Talent] Govern talent location and mobility data quality — object: Talent Data Quality (Location); trigger: Monthly DQ inspection; quarterly mobility review; owners: Manager Talent; agents: VANGUARD, TIDE, ECHO; kind: governance
  Govern completeness and freshness of location + relocation fields on the talent profile; inspect coverage by BU, geo, and band; chase stale or missing entries; surface mobility supply heatmap
- [Talent] Govern master-data domains and source-of-truth — object: Master Data Policy; trigger: Annual policy refresh; new system in scope; owners: Manager Sales Ops; agents: ORBIT, ATLAS; kind: governance
  Govern domain owners and golden-record definitions for Account, Contact, Lead, Opportunity, Project, FRF, Solution, Contract; publish source-of-truth matrix and update rules
### Stage 2: Opportunity Qualification
- [Projects] Run customer credit-risk check — object: Customer Credit Check; trigger: Net-new customer at qualification; expansion above credit threshold; owners: Finance, Manager Finance; agents: LEDGER, BULWARK, WARDEN; kind: decision
  Finance runs credit / financial-health check on prospective customer — D&B / credit-bureau pull, payment history on existing engagements, sanctions / OFAC screen; surface credit risk score and payment-term guardrails to deal-shape and commercial-structuring teams
### Stage 3: Solution Strategy
- [Revenue & Billing] Track solution win-rate / pipeline / margin — object: Solution Performance; trigger: Monthly portfolio review; owners: Manager Practices; agents: CONDUIT, PRISM, ECHO; kind: action
  Inspect each solution / archetype on pipeline contribution, win rate, average deal size, delivery margin, and competitive posture; rebalance solution investment
### Stage 4: Deal Shaping
- [Talent] Submit FRF (Forecast Resource Request) — object: FRF; trigger: Deal-shaping team finalized; owners: Markets, Practices, Delivery; agents: FORGE, VANGUARD; kind: trigger
  Submit resource request to TA / RMG with role, skill, ramp date, bill-rate band, and full location-of-work block (city, country, timezone, on-site / hybrid / remote, travel %, bill-to country, visa / work-permit requirement) — created by Markets, Practices, or Delivery during shape
- [Talent] Capture capacity, skill and location requirements on FRF — object: FRF (Capacity + Skill + Location Requirement); trigger: FRF creation; scope, ramp, or client-site change; owners: Markets, Practices, Delivery; agents: FORGE, VANGUARD, TIDE; kind: trigger
  Capture client-mandated demand for each resource line — capacity (headcount, FTE / allocation %, ramp-up curve, peak vs steady-state, start date, duration, end date, billable hours per week, shift coverage); skill (role / level / years of experience, primary technical skill stack, must-have certifications, domain or industry experience, language proficiency, security clearance); and location (onsite city / country, allowed remote / hybrid mix, mandatory travel days, time-zone overlap window, bill-to country, visa / work-authorization requirements, client-site security or badging constraints)
- [Talent] Dedupe FRF on submission — object: FRF (Dedup Match); trigger: FRF submit event; owners: Markets, Practices, Delivery, Talent; agents: VANGUARD, FORGE; kind: decision
  Match new FRF against open / recent FRFs on same opportunity + account by role family, skill stack, location-of-work, and ramp window; block exact duplicates, flag overlapping demand for consolidation, and link related FRFs into a single demand bundle for the Talent queue
- [Talent] Match resources to opportunity by skill — object: Resource Match; trigger: FRF submitted; owners: Talent; agents: VANGUARD; kind: decision
  System matches available resources to opportunity skill requirements; surfaces best-fit candidates
- [Talent] Match FRF demand to talent supply by location — object: Resource Match (Location); trigger: FRF queued for fulfillment; owners: Talent, Manager Talent; agents: VANGUARD, TIDE; kind: decision
  Match FRF location-of-work requirement against talent supply — local-bench resources first, then willing-to-relocate resources scored against destination eligibility, visa fit, family / dependent constraints, and earliest available date; surface gap heatmap and short-term travel-from-home options
- [Talent] Flag location-gap risk and propose mitigations — object: FRF (Location Risk); trigger: Location gap detected on FRF; owners: Manager Talent, Practices, Delivery; agents: VANGUARD, TIDE, SENTINEL, FORGE; kind: decision
  Flag FRFs where local supply is insufficient and propose mitigations — relocate willing resource, sub-contract local talent, hire-to-fill, nearshore / offshore split, client-approved remote ratio, or rebadge — with cost and timeline impact for deal-shape review
- [Talent] Acknowledge talent demand / FRF intake — object: FRF; trigger: FRF submitted; owners: Talent; agents: VANGUARD; kind: trigger
  Talent team receives notification of talent demand from deal-shape FRF; ack and queue
- [Talent] Inspect FRF queue and manage resourcing risks — object: FRF Queue; trigger: Daily FRF queue review; owners: Manager Talent; agents: VANGUARD; kind: action

- [Revenue & Billing] Draft pricing and margin sheets — object: Pricing Worksheet; trigger: Scope and effort baseline ready; owners: Markets, Practices; agents: VAULT; kind: action

- [Projects] Update risk register — object: Opportunity Risk; trigger: Risk surfaced during shape; owners: Markets, Practices, Delivery; agents: SENTINEL, BULWARK; kind: governance

- [Talent] Forecast resource demand by skill / role / geo — object: Resource Demand Plan; trigger: Weekly demand-supply cycle; owners: Manager Talent; agents: VANGUARD, FORGE, COMPASS; kind: action

- [Talent] Track bench and resource availability — object: Resource Bench; trigger: Allocation event; weekly review; owners: Talent; agents: VANGUARD; kind: action
